chunks: Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said:
I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام at Minā when a man came and said, 'Some people have arrived, and the hajj has passed them by.'

He عليه السلام said: 'We ask Allah for well-being. I hold that each man among them should slaughter a sheep, come out of iḥrām, and hajj remains due upon them the following year if they return to their homelands. But if they remain in Mecca until the days of Tashrīq have passed, then go out to the mīqāt of the people of Mecca, enter into iḥrām from there, and perform an ʿumrah, then hajj is not due upon them the following year.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: the days of Tashrīq, marking the timing mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.اعْتَمَرُوا: they perform ʿumrah, which affects the next year's obligation
key_terms.الْحَجُّ: the hajj pilgrimage, whose missed performance is the subject of the ruling
key_terms.الْعَافِيَةَ: well-being, invoked in the Imam's opening statement
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Mecca, where they remain until a specified time
key_terms.شَاةً: a sheep to be slaughtered as required in this case
key_terms.فَأَحْرَمُوا: they enter into iḥrām from the designated point

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who arrives after missing the hajj rites?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for those who miss hajj after arriving. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that they should offer a sheep and exit iḥrām, and in some cases they must perform hajj the following year, while in another case performing ʿumrah in the described manner removes that obligation.
